closure_classes.proved: a theorem in the record (including exact equivalences)
closure_classes.obstruction_proved: a theorem that rules a class of arguments or objects out, on stated hypotheses
closure_classes.counterexample: an explicit object refuting a statement on an exact domain
closure_classes.finite_outcome: an exact computation with a stated finite domain
closure_classes.attempt_closed: a route that stalled, used too weak an estimate or stopped, with no proof that it cannot work
closure_classes.superseded: a route replaced by an equivalent or stronger formulation
closure_classes.out_of_support: a route the record names or implies but never tried

reading_rule: Only proved, obstruction_proved, counterexample and finite_outcome close anything, and only on their own hypotheses, domain and representation. An attempt_closed route keeps its parent idea eligible until the cause of the stall is located; an out_of_support route is unknown, not failed. Checked results are premises in every world.

R2.transport: a structurally different engine for A19: Schlickewei's p-adic Subspace Theorem in S-unit coordinates, never tried in the chain records (D09)
R2.result: transcendence of the Lambert subsum over every infinite divisibility chain at every rational base a/b > 1 (ordinary proof citing the Subspace Theorem)

R3.transport: C09 (Erdos's 1948 divisibility argument, stalled for the totient because the coefficients are as large as n) repaired by reducing the coefficients and building 2-divisible blocks from prime factors of Fermat numbers
R3.result: for a_n = phi(n) mod 2^kappa(n) with 2^kappa(n) = o(log n), the series sum a_n 2^-n is rational exactly when a_n = 0 for all large n; it is irrational whenever kappa(3^k) >= 2 infinitely often (ordinary proof; extends the bounded-residue theorem of the #249 short paper to slowly growing moduli)
